headline: Week over week: subs 16→20, views 6,169→8,511 (+38%). Ep 5's retention curve validates the new edit/recording defaults — 8:52 avg view duration, the channel's best, with early retention ~2x Eps 1–4. Two red flags own the week: Ep 6 launched into a 3-day dead clip queue and is impression-starved (77 impressions / 21 views in 3 days vs Ep 5's 1,660 / 45), and longform packaging is the broken link — YouTube serves big impressions (8.8K on the Ep 2 clip) but sub-1% CTR; retitles alone didn't fix it, thumbnails are next.

production.title: Fix longform packaging: impressions are there, CTR isn't — add custom thumbnails
production.evidence: Reach data landed (36 videos). Longform clips get real impression volume but terrible CTR: Ep 2 clip 8,833 impressions @ 0.42% (most-served video on the channel), Ep 4 OpenUSD clip 3,854 @ 1.95%, Ep 5 clones clip 792 @ 0.38%, burn desk 369 @ 0.54%. Episodes are only okay: Ep 3 3.44%, Ep 4 2.93%, Ep 1 2.26%, Ep 5 just 1.2% on 1,660 impressions. All of these run auto-generated thumbnails. The retitle experiment's verdict: titles fixed the convention but aggregate CTR stayed sub-2% on 5 of 7 longforms — the thumbnail is the remaining variable.
production.recommendation: Add a branded custom-thumbnail step (face + 3–5 word hook text, brand colors) to the publishing flow for every episode and longform clip; shorts don't need it. Start with the two highest-impression laggards (Ep 2 clip, Ep 4 OpenUSD clip) and the Ep 5 episode as the test set.
production.status_note: New this week — first actionable output of the impressions/CTR data.

production.title: Never launch an episode into a dead clip queue — bracket every launch
production.evidence: The Ep 5 clip queue ended Jul 16 and Ep 6 clips didn't start until Jul 20, leaving Jul 17–19 empty. Daily channel views collapsed into that gap (49 → 12 → 15) and Ep 6 published into the trough on Sat Jul 18: 77 impressions and 21 views in its first 3 days, vs Ep 5's 1,660 impressions / 45 views (and a 170-view channel day on its Fri-night launch). The algorithm had nothing warm to recommend the episode from.
production.recommendation: Schedule each episode's first short for the morning of episode day and keep the daily 2 PM queue unbroken across the episode boundary (stretch the outgoing batch or cut a pre-release teaser from the new episode). Consider pinning the episode publish slot to the Thu-night/Fri slot that worked for Eps 1–5 rather than Saturday afternoon.
production.status_note: New this week. Ep 6's launch window is already lost; apply to Ep 7.

production.title: Wire the shorts→episode funnel — it's still mostly unwired, and it's still the weakest metric
production.evidence: SHORTS traffic grew 4,525→7,305 views (86% of channel) but only 462 watch-minutes and ~2 lifetime subs from shorts; episodes still do the converting (SUBSCRIBER+direct: 525 views but 1,072 watch-min). Encouraging: RELATED_VIDEO watch-minutes tripled (67→206 min on 86 views) — the few wired links do work. The manual steps (related-video, pinned comments, end screens) remain undone for the live Ep 5 and Ep 6 batches.
production.recommendation: Do the funnel checklist for the Ep 5 + Ep 6 batches in one Studio session (related video, pinned comment with episode link + timestamp, end screens). It's ~30 min of clicking and the only channel lever that's pure execution, no creative.
production.status_note: Tooling done since 7/11 (yt_upload.py checklist + lint). Manual wiring still pending for Ep 5 and Ep 6 batches — carried over two weeks now.

production.title: Retention-informed edit defaults are working — keep them
production.evidence: Ep 5, the first cut under the new defaults, posts the channel's best long-form engagement: 8:52 avg view duration (Ep 1 6:47, Ep 2 6:10, Ep 4 4:37, Ep 3 2:59) and 25.6% retention at the 5% mark vs 11–19% for Eps 1–4. The curve holds a long plateau (16–19% absolute) from 15% clear through 55% of a 61-min runtime, and vs-typical peaks 0.62 in the AI-clones panel and 0.68 when the perp fill lands. Ep 6 doubled down (56:12 runtime, 47s 4-clip cold open, first segment at 2:05) — its curve lands next week.
production.recommendation: No change: keep cold-open-from-best-moment + first-segment-by-2-min + 45–55 min target. Judge Ep 6's curve against Ep 5's next pull.
production.status_note: Defaults in podcast-video-edit SKILL.md since 7/11; Ep 5 curve is the first confirming evidence. Retire once Ep 6's curve confirms.

production.title: Clip titling convention — done and holding
production.evidence: Zero 'Highlight -' titles remain live (all 7 longforms now '<Hook> - Ep N Clip' or hook-only). Note: Ep 5's episode was also retitled live ('We Gave an AI $100 and It Bet On War' → 'Our AI Clones Have Faces Now (This Is Getting Worse)') — presumably chasing its weak 1.2% CTR; segment-times.md updated to match.
production.recommendation: Nothing left to do; convention + lint live in clipify. CTR ownership moves to the thumbnail item above.
production.status_note: Complete as of this week — retire next review.

recording.title: Check-in discipline improved — now move the gamer-thumb saga out of minutes 2–4
recording.evidence: Ep 5's welcome ran 0:43–1:46 (inside the ≤60s target) and early retention doubled vs Eps 1–4 (25.6% vs 11–19% at the 5% mark). But the thumb saga occupied 1:46–4:26 and the curve bleeds straight through it (30.2% → 23.3%). Ep 6 cut it to 48 seconds (1:17–2:05) — right instinct.
recording.recommendation: Keep the check-in ≤60s. Retainer bits like the thumb saga work better as mid-show palate cleansers than as minute-2 content — record them self-contained so the edit can place them.

recording.title: The ≤8-minute explainer cap keeps being proven right — Ep 5 violated it once and paid
recording.evidence: Ep 5's only sustained decay is exactly the 10.3-min 'Not all USDC is the same: chain drift' explainer (33:53–44:12): absolute retention slides 16.3% → 11.6% and vs-typical craters 0.44 → 0.19, the episode's worst band. Everything before it held flat for 20 minutes. Same pattern as Ep 4's L2 deep-dive and Ep 2's perps explainer.
recording.recommendation: Hard cap explainers at 8 minutes and tie them to live stakes. Chain drift had a natural stake ('your burrito money') — surfacing the stake first and cutting the mechanism detail would likely have held the plateau.

recording.title: AI bits and live stakes remain the retention spine — keep pulling them earlier
recording.evidence: Ep 5's vs-typical climbs from 0.28 to 0.62 through the AI-Venice segment + panel react (4:26–18:56) — putting an AI bit in the first 10 minutes worked exactly as predicted. The perp fill at 50:45 bumps vs-typical to 0.68 with 85% of the runtime gone. Perp of Fortune moved from 27:08 (Ep 5) to 18:26 (Ep 6) — progress, still not first-10-minutes.
recording.recommendation: Keep one of the three anchors (AI bit / live stakes / confession) in the first 10 minutes. The confession experiment from last review still hasn't happened — Ep 6 had none; bring one to Ep 7.
